newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK leader frontrunner wants chief secretary to stay.
newsitem.headline: HK leader frontrunner wants chief secretary to stay.

text.p: Shipping magnate Tung Chee-hwa, the man regarded as heir-apparent to Governor Chris Patten, told reporters on Monday he hoped Hong Kong's top civil servant would remain in her post after next year's handover of sovereignty.
"I hope that Mrs Chan can stay on," he said of the Chief Secretary.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30, 1997, when the governor will be replaced by a chief executive appointed by a China-backed Selection Committee.

Tung scored a landslide on Friday in the first round of the 400-strong Selection Committee's ballot to choose the chief executive and many in the territory believe he is on the brink of being named Hong Kong's new leader.
Tung is the choice of the powerful business lobby and his popularity would rise further if he were to team up with Chan, who is held in high regard in Hong Kong.
Opinion polls consistently rated her as the "people's choice" for chief executive. Chan declined to stand but has offered to stay on in her current post -- a move that would require China's approval.
Tung said Chan had phoned him to offer her congratulations on his performance last Friday when he scored 206 of the 400 votes cast in the first round of balloting.
The runner up, former chief justice Yang Ti Liang, who polled 82 votes, told reporters he had not received a congratulatory call from Chan.
The final run-off for the post is scheduled for December 11.
